review_summary: All four stated fixes are present in the document text. One newly discovered issue: the reserved-pattern citation resolves to a function whose current body contains no such validation, making the cited location an untested assumption rather than a verified insertion point.

issues.title: Reserved-pattern validation not present at cited line range
issues.description: The design states: 'The validation lives in `Evaluation::from_yaml_str` ([src/content/evaluation.rs:166-171])'. Lines 166-171 of that file are the existing `from_yaml_str` body: an empty-string guard followed by `serde_yaml_ng::from_str`. There is no `^case-\d+$` regex check, no new `EvaluationError` variant for the reserved-pattern rejection, and no post-deserialization validation loop. The citation presents the validation as already identified at a concrete location, but the location contains only the existing deserialization path. The fifth sub-test that asserts 'a parse error naming the reserved-pattern rule' will therefore fail to compile until both a new error variant and a new post-deserialization check are added, neither of which is specified in the design.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify that `from_yaml_str` is the function where the validation must be added, not where it currently lives. Specify that a new `EvaluationError` variant (e.g. `ReservedCaseName { name: String }`) must be introduced to carry the rejection reason, because the existing variants (`Empty`, `Parse`, `Emit`) cover only deserialization failures, not post-deserialization semantic checks. If the validator is a private helper called by `from_yaml_str`, name it in the design so the implementer has an unambiguous insertion point.
